scope.localization_input: A reproduced async failure plus a FlakeSync-style critical point, barrier point, expected completion multiplicity, and witnessed failure-inducing schedule.
scope.claim_boundary: This document specifies a candidate-generation and acceptance contract. It is not evidence that a new repair technique already exists or outperforms FlakeSync.

verdict_lattice.pass: Every applicable property has positive evidence under the frozen validation scenarios and no prohibited structural fact is present.
verdict_lattice.fail: At least one direct contract violation or dynamically witnessed failure exists.
verdict_lattice.unknown: No failure has been established, but at least one required property lacks a valid or supported probe.

overall.unresolved: no property fails and one or more properties are unknown

properties.name: artifact integrity and buildability
properties.requirement: Generation is transactional: all intended edits are emitted, the clean source is restored, the diff reapplies to the pinned revision, and the affected module compiles.
static_checks: parse every emitted diff and require at least one real hunk
reject absolute or unresolved diff targets in the distributable patch
reject partial multi-file output, leaked backup files, and dirty restoration
AST-parse changed Java files before publishing the candidate
dynamic_checks: git-apply check on a clean pinned revision
affected-module compilation using the recorded environment
project formatting and mandatory quality gates where available
properties.failure_oracle: Any internal exception, missing file, dirty workspace, apply failure, compilation failure, or required quality-gate failure rejects the candidate; a zero Maven exit alone is insufficient.

properties.name: ordinary behavior preservation
properties.requirement: The original target oracle and relevant ordinary behavior remain visible without perturbation.
static_checks: retain the defining assertion or replace it only with a demonstrably equivalent stronger oracle
flag production-code test hooks and unrelated API changes
record changed files, methods, public APIs, and assertion edits
dynamic_checks: ten fresh ordinary target executions
target class or nearest relevant sibling selection
affected module tests and project quality gates where feasible
properties.failure_oracle: Any target non-pass, hidden worker exception, deleted or weakened oracle, or differential ordinary regression rejects the candidate.

properties.name: causal effectiveness
properties.requirement: The repair prevents the exact reproduced failure because it enforces the required causal completion, not merely because a later rerun happened to pass.
static_checks: map the awaited condition to the critical event and original assertion
reject synchronization on an event that can occur before the asserted state is safe
record the critical, barrier, threshold, delay, and source revision in the candidate manifest
dynamic_checks: matched unpatched and patched executions under the same recorded perturbation
durable witnesses that the delay, critical update, barrier wait, and target test executed
hold-out perturbations around the same causal interval when available
properties.failure_oracle: The unpatched control must reproduce the defining failure with witnessed perturbation and the patched execution must pass with the same witnessed perturbation; otherwise effectiveness is failed or unknown, never assumed.

properties.name: bounded progress
properties.requirement: The waiter has a semantic deadline and a diagnostic failure path when a producer fails, never starts, never publishes, or publishes only part of the expected completion set.
static_checks: reject unbounded while loops and deadline-free awaits
require a monotonic deadline or a bounded concurrency API
require a timeout message naming the awaited event and observed state
dynamic_checks: suppress publication immediately before the synchronization event
throw from the producer immediately before publication
omit producer start where the harness supports it
withhold one of multiple required completions
properties.failure_oracle: The repair must terminate through its own bounded diagnostic before the outer harness deadline. An outer process timeout is a repair failure, not acceptable timeout handling.

properties.name: memory and multi-writer safety
properties.requirement: Cross-thread publication has a Java happens-before edge and multi-writer updates cannot be lost, duplicated, or counted before causal completion.
static_checks: reject plain shared fields used for cross-thread publication
reject volatile compound updates such as counter++
require Future, CompletableFuture, CountDownLatch, Phaser, join, lock/condition, or an equivalent documented primitive
verify that expected multiplicity and exactly-once completion are well defined
dynamic_checks: deterministic post-read/pre-write rendezvous for counter-like updates
two or more natural writers where the subject exposes them
partial, duplicate, and reordered writer completion scenarios
properties.failure_oracle: Any confirmed lost update, premature release, duplicate satisfaction, visibility violation, or unsound multiplicity rejects the candidate. Absence of a second writer is unknown rather than a pass.

properties.name: invocation isolation and noninterference
properties.requirement: Synchronization state belongs to one operation or test invocation and cannot be observed or satisfied by an earlier, neighboring, or parallel invocation.
static_checks: reject process-wide mutable synchronization state
require local or uniquely keyed per-invocation state
construct the synchronization object before workers can publish
require cleanup on every normal and exceptional exit
dynamic_checks: fresh-JVM target execution
sequential repeated execution in a reused JVM
neighboring test or target-class execution
same-test and peer-test parallel execution with confirmed execution witnesses
early publication before the barrier begins waiting
properties.failure_oracle: A differential neighboring, reused-JVM, or parallel non-pass, a stale/early signal satisfying the wrong invocation, or direct global-state leakage rejects the candidate. Unsupported or unconfirmed execution remains unknown.

properties.name: cancellation, interruption, and cleanup
properties.requirement: An active waiter responds to cancellation, preserves the interrupted status or propagates InterruptedException, and releases temporary resources and hooks.
static_checks: require an explicit interruption path
require re-interruption when InterruptedException is converted to an assertion failure
require finally or teardown cleanup for listeners, tasks, and scoped state
dynamic_checks: suppress the completion publication without terminating the producer
directly interrupt the thread inside the generated wait
cancel outstanding futures or shut down the executor where supported
properties.failure_oracle: Both intervention witnesses must be present; the waiter must terminate within its semantic deadline, preserve cancellation semantics, and leave no live worker or hook.

properties.name: behavioral fidelity and oracle preservation
properties.requirement: The repair preserves the test's intended assertion and propagates causal worker failures instead of making the test green by weakening behavior.
static_checks: diff assertions and expected exceptions
flag catch-and-ignore blocks, removed checks, widened tolerances, and disabled tests
record test-only changes to production code and public APIs
dynamic_checks: inject a worker exception and require it to reach the test outcome
run unchanged neighboring assertions
compare failure type and diagnostics with the unpatched defining failure
properties.failure_oracle: Assertion suppression, exception swallowing, unjustified tolerance widening, or success after a witnessed causal worker failure rejects the candidate.

properties.name: repeatability under positive and counter-scenarios
properties.requirement: The preceding properties hold for the declared number of independent executions and targeted counter-scenarios.
static_checks: freeze commands, seeds, resources, bounds, stopping rules, and evidence requirements before execution
hash every candidate and validation input
dynamic_checks: paper-style 100-run confirmation when claiming reproduction of the paper oracle
ten ordinary source-patch runs
five matched recorded-delay pairs when the first pair does not already fail
deterministic targeted counter-scenarios with durable intervention witnesses
properties.failure_oracle: Stop at the first non-pass for an all-runs-pass claim. A successful rerun never erases an earlier preserved counterexample.

ordered_strategy.strategy: reuse an existing causal completion abstraction
examples: Future.get with a semantic timeout and exception propagation
CountDownLatch await with a justified count and timeout
Thread.join with a timeout and postcondition
existing callback, listener, condition, or domain state transition

ordered_strategy.strategy: introduce an invocation-local bounded synchronization object
requirements: created before any producer can publish
passed through an existing scoped object or a minimal typed interface
semantic deadline, interrupt propagation, exception propagation, and finally cleanup
no static mutable state and no generic production test hook

ordered_strategy.strategy: bounded polling of a domain predicate
requirements: predicate directly implies the assertion's safety
monotonic deadline based on project or domain semantics
sleep or blocking wait rather than Thread.yield spinning
original assertion retained after the poll
used when no invocation-local causal observable or defensible deadline exists
emit a diagnostic explaining the unsatisfied contract instead of an unsafe patch

timeout_selection_priority: project configuration already governing the asynchronous operation
test framework or test annotation deadline
otherwise abstain rather than synthesize an arbitrary sleep multiplier
transaction: parse and bind the exact source revision and localization tuple
generate edits in a disposable workspace
reapply the diff to a fresh clean workspace
compile before admitting the candidate to dynamic validation
publish success only after all preceding checks pass

counter_scenarios.name: recorded failure schedule
counter_scenarios.intervention: Apply the exact recorded delay to matched unpatched and patched executions.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: Unpatched fails with the defining oracle; patched passes.

counter_scenarios.name: producer exception before publication
counter_scenarios.intervention: Throw from the producer immediately before the completion publication.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: Bounded diagnostic failure that exposes the worker exception.

counter_scenarios.name: missing or never-started producer
counter_scenarios.intervention: Prevent producer start or suppress every completion event without killing the test process.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: The repair's own deadline fires before the outer harness bound.

counter_scenarios.name: early signal
counter_scenarios.intervention: Deliver the completion after the causal event but before the barrier starts waiting.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: The invocation-local synchronization retains the event; no reset erases it.

counter_scenarios.name: partial multiple completion
counter_scenarios.intervention: Allow fewer than the declared number of causal producers to complete.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: Bounded diagnostic reports the missing completion; no premature assertion.

counter_scenarios.name: two-writer collision
counter_scenarios.intervention: Rendezvous two natural writers after reading shared state and before publication/update.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: No completion is lost and release occurs only after the declared causal set.

counter_scenarios.name: waiter interruption
counter_scenarios.intervention: Hold completion and interrupt the thread while it is inside the repair wait.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: Bounded exit with propagated or preserved interruption and cleanup.

counter_scenarios.name: sequential reused-JVM invocation
counter_scenarios.intervention: Run target and a compatible peer sequentially in one test JVM in both orders.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: Neither invocation consumes stale completion state from the other.

counter_scenarios.name: neighboring test class or suite
counter_scenarios.intervention: Run the target class or nearest affected suite with matched unpatched control.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: No differential failure, hang, or changed assertion.

counter_scenarios.name: parallel same-test and peer-test invocation
counter_scenarios.intervention: Execute two invocation identities concurrently with explicit start and completion witnesses.
counter_scenarios.expected_reliable_outcome: Each invocation is satisfied only by its own causal completion and both remain bounded.

development_and_test_split.development_evidence: The current 20-artifact exposure cohort may be used to derive the contract and detectors.
development_and_test_split.held_out_requirement: Freeze a separate case roster before implementing or tuning the new generator; do not substitute cases after observing outcomes.
development_and_test_split.reason: Evaluating only on the cases that motivated the contract would overstate generalization.

arms: independent developer fix where a strict comparator exists
controlled_inputs: same pinned source revision and module
same target test and defining assertion
same critical point, barrier point, threshold, delay, and resource envelope
same validation commands, bounds, witnesses, and stopping rules
primary_outcomes: complete nine-property contract pass per case
causal repair among cases with valid matched controls
bounded diagnostic outcome under every supported negative-progress scenario
repair abstention instead of unsafe patch generation
secondary_outcomes: patch size, changed files, public API surface, and production intrusion
reporting_units: independent repair design or normalized template

statistics.current_cohort: Report exact descriptive numerators and eligible denominators. Do not use independent-case binomial confidence intervals because cases are clustered by project and template.
statistics.future_comparison: Use paired case-level outcomes between repair arms, report project/design clusters, and preregister any inferential model after the held-out roster is known.
statistics.missingness: Report not reached, unsupported, inconclusive intervention, pass, and fail separately.

stopping_and_bounds.all_runs_pass_claim: Stop at the first non-pass and retain it as the terminal counterexample.
stopping_and_bounds.outer_bound: Use the frozen calibrated process bound as a harness backstop; the repair's semantic timeout must expire first.
stopping_and_bounds.adaptive_extension: Increase a cap only when durable evidence shows forward progress, the preregistered intervention has not already produced a decisive witness, and the original bounded outcome remains preserved.
stopping_and_bounds.no_extension_after_counterexample: Do not extend a cap after the required intervention witnesses are present and the frozen timeout outcome has occurred.

non_guarantees: Finite testing cannot prove correctness under every Java schedule.
The contract cannot repair an incorrect critical/barrier localization without additional localization evidence.
A dynamically calibrated deadline is not automatically a semantically correct deadline.
Static detectors do not replace whole-program race or liveness verification.
Passing the declared scenarios does not prove absence of regressions outside the exercised module and environment.
No safe invocation-local observable may be accessible without an unacceptable production redesign; the correct result is then abstention.
